_note: Terrain grid for the Western Canada (CPR, 1881-87) map. RESCALE (2nd pass): 24 cols x 20 rows, pointy-top odd-r, hex radius 40 -- replaces the original 40x34/radius-24 grid because that grid's hex distances (Winnipeg-Calgary 26, Calgary-Vancouver 17, Winnipeg-Vancouver 43) made the connection-bonus mechanic completely dead (0 of 16 measured games ever paid it -- docs/western-canada-board-balance-measurement.md). Compressing the same real lon/lat footprint onto far fewer grid cells (docs/western-canada-rescale-prototype.md's spike, promoted here properly) brings Calgary-Vancouver down to a workable ~10 hexes without changing which real-world area the board covers. Of the 20 rows, only rows 0-17 hold any mainland city; rows 18-19 are a deliberate buffer that exists purely to give the Vancouver Island cluster room to sit south of the mainland with a real off-map gap between them -- see the water-gap region below and project.mjs's header comment. The grid was generated (scripts/western/gen-terrain.mjs, kept for reference/regeneration) from a hand-specified route network mirroring the real CPR mainline and its branches, terrain-typed by re-derived region rules (not resized from the old grid's thresholds), then the Vancouver Island water gap was hand-carved on top and verified: removing its single bridge hex (1,16) disconnects exactly the 7-hex island cluster from the other 196 tiles (checked by BFS, and mirrored in index.html's WC self-test). Legend: O = off-map (water, wilderness, or panel space), P = plains, F = forest, M = mountain, C = city (the city itself comes from cities.json, which must place a city on every C -- see build-map.mjs, which stamps 'terrain:city' over whatever base letter is here; the letter only has to not be 'O').

regions._note: Why each area is the terrain it is. Purely documentation — the generator/build script reads only `grid`. Re-derived for the 24x22 rescale from where the actual cities in cities.json sit (not resized from the old 40x34 thresholds, and not eyeballed — see gen-terrain.mjs's terrainFor()).
regions.Northern boreal arc: Rows 0-6. Forest. Edmonton (9,2), Battleford (13,5) and Prince Albert (15,3) all sit in this band, off the CPR mainline proper — matching the research doc's note that this area saw very little of the real 1881-87 construction story and should read as sparse, low-value scenery, same choice as the Canadian board's Shield interior.
regions.Rockies and Selkirks chokepoint: Cols 3-10, rows 7-12. Mountain. Every one of Cochrane (7,7), Field (6,8), Calgary (8,9), Revelstoke (5,10), Gleichen (10,10), Banff (6,11), Kamloops (3,11) and Golden (5,12) lands inside this box — the single hardest and most expensive stretch of the whole railway, per the research doc's terrain section. Fort Macleod and Lethbridge (both row 13) sit deliberately just outside it: prairie/foothills towns, not mountain towns.
regions.Fraser Canyon: Cols 0-3, rows 11-14. Mountain, shading toward plains at Kamloops (already in the box above). Onderdonk's Fraser Canyon contract — Yale (2,13) sits right in this band.
regions.Lower Mainland lowlands: Cols 0-3, rows 15-17. Plains. Vancouver, Port Moody, New Westminster and the near shore — flat lowland delta country opening onto the Strait of Georgia.
regions.Vancouver Island water gap: The Strait of Georgia, hand-carved rather than auto-generated. Row 16 is off-map at every column except (1,16) — a single bridge hex directly adjacent to BOTH Vancouver (1,15) and Nanaimo (0,17), mirroring how the original 40x34 board's Charlottetown/Sydney-style crossings worked, just re-measured for this grid. Column 3 at row 16 carries an unrelated mainland-only connector (Port Moody <-> New Westminster) that does not touch the island. Row 17 is off-map at column 1 and row 18 is off-map at columns 2-3, specifically closing a 'back door' the automatic route-padding first produced (New Westminster reaching Nanaimo's island interior without ever crossing the bridge). Verified by BFS: removing (1,16) alone disconnects exactly the 7-hex island cluster (Nanaimo + Victoria + Esquimalt + their connecting tiles) from the other 196 tiles — a real, load-bearing single point of failure, not just an unused hex. See docs/western-canada-board-rescale-final.md for the full hex-by-hex accounting.
regions.Vancouver Island: Cols 0-3, rows 17-19, reached only through the bridge above. Nanaimo sits right at the crossing (row 17); Victoria and Esquimalt sit one row further south (row 19, two columns apart at cols 0 and 2) — the whole island cluster is compressed into 3 rows rather than the mainland-side rows' usual spread, specifically so it stays clear of the printed company-plates strip at the bottom of the frame. Reached, in reality, never by the CPR itself (the Esquimalt & Nanaimo Railway was a separate, independently-owned company in this era).
regions.Prairie corridor: Everything else still standing (Manitoba, Saskatchewan/Assiniboia, and Alberta east of the foothills). Plains — the flat-to-rolling country that let Van Horne's crews lay 500+ miles in a single season (1882).
